Find the inverse functions $f^{-1}(x)$ and $g^{-1}(x)$:
$$y = 4x - 2 \implies x = \frac{y + 2}{4} \implies f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x + 2}{4}$$
$$y = \frac{4}{x + 1} \implies x + 1 = \frac{4}{y} \implies g^{-1}(x) = \frac{4}{x} - 1 = \frac{4 - x}{x}$$

Equate the two inverse functions:
$$\frac{x + 2}{4} = \frac{4 - x}{x}$$

Cross-multiply and form a quadratic equation in $x$:
$$x(x + 2) = 4(4 - x) \implies x^2 + 2x = 16 - 4x \implies x^2 + 6x - 16 = 0$$

Factorise and solve for $x$:
$$(x + 8)(x - 2) = 0 \implies x = 2 \quad\text{or}\quad x = -8$$
